records.evidence: no deterministic engine for strategy_id 'trend_pullback_call_v1' (engine-registered: current_control_v1, directional_spread_v1, range_hv_iron_condor_v1)
expected_failure_modes: Regime flip immediately after entry: TREND_HV can decay into RANGE_HV or RANGE_LV within days, turning a momentum continuation into a theta bleed or a repeated-stop chop.
The pullback is actually the start of a reversal; repeated 1% structure-based stop-outs accumulate faster than the occasional winner, producing negative expectancy.
The VIX premium cap excludes too many valid trending setups, collapsing the trade count below the 20-trade minimum and forcing a NOT_RELIABLE classification.
ADX in high-volatility regimes is lagging and noisy, admitting entries that look like strong trends but immediately mean-revert.
records.hypothesis: In TREND_HV regimes, high-volatility trending markets show momentum persistence; continuation moves after a controlled pullback are more reliable than breakout entries, which suffer from false breakouts and poor fills. Buying an ATM call on a pullback to the 20-EMA while the uptrend structure stays intact (spot above EMA50, EMA20 above EMA50, ADX confirming trend strength, RSI cooled into a neutral band) prices the entry closer to support, reducing the distance to the structure- based stop. Capping the VIX premium zone below RICH/HIGH/PANIC keeps long-premium theta bleed manageable, since expensive implied vol typically reverts and damages long premium even if spot moves in the direction of the trade.
records.research_question: Over the frozen window (2025-08-13..2026-08-13), does a TREND_HV-only pullback long call on NIFTY - defined as spot above EMA50, EMA20 above EMA50, ADX > 25, RSI in 45..55, VIX_ZONE not RICH/HIGH/PANIC and PCR <= 1.1 - produce a positive net expectancy with at least 20 trades on the out-of-sample slice (exits on/after 2026-03-01), and does it differ materially from the current_control_v1 baseline?
records.title: Trend-persistence pullback long call (TREND_HV, VIX-capped)

records.evidence: no deterministic engine for strategy_id 'range_fade_stretch_v1' (engine-registered: current_control_v1, directional_spread_v1, range_hv_iron_condor_v1)
expected_failure_modes: Regime lag: RANGE_HV at the signal close transitions to TREND_HV in the following sessions, the fade is counter-trend, and the short call is exercised to the wing-width maximum loss.
Gap risk: an overnight gap beyond the sold strike removes the reversion window, and the spread realizes its maximum loss on the entry session.

Cost and theta drag: four orders per round trip at the canonical cost model plus slippage exceed the average reversion credit, and shallow stretches revert only partially, leaving no edge at the minimum sample size.
records.hypothesis: In a RANGE_HV regime NIFTY prints wide, mean-reverting swings rather than sustained runs. When the daily close stretches beyond the VIX-implied expected-move band while RSI reads 72 or above, the impulse is typically locally exhausted and price tends to revert toward the band center and the heavy OI / max-pain zone. Entering a defined-risk call credit spread at that stretch expresses the reversion with a capped wing-width loss while theta decays the short leg in the seller's favour. The regime gate and VIX window keep the fade out of fresh trends and out of a too-cheap premium tape. It might fail because RANGE_HV classification lags the close: a range that is actually breaking into a trend produces follow-through instead of reversion, and because the thin credit net of a four-order cost model may not cover the losing trades.
records.research_question: Over the frozen window with the dev/OOS split at 2026-03-01, does entering one NIFTY call credit spread per signal (REGIME equals RANGE_HV, RSI at or above 72, VIX between 16 and 25) that targets reversion to the VIX-implied expected-move band and the max-pain zone produce at least 20 trades and a win rate and profit factor on both splits that exceed current_control_v1 under the canonical cost model?
records.title: RANGE_HV overbought-stretch fade: defined-risk NIFTY call credit spread reverting to the VIX band and max pain

records.evidence: no deterministic engine for strategy_id 'maxpain_brokenwing_condor_v1' (engine-registered: current_control_v1, directional_spread_v1, range_hv_iron_condor_v1)
expected_failure_modes: Trend continuation in TREND_HV drives spot through the short strikes at expiry; the wide insurance wing is breached for near its full width and such losses cluster on the highest-credit entries.
The entry gate is too restrictive (TREND_HV + VIX >= 16 + PCR <= 0.95), yielding fewer than 20 trades in the window and classifying the result NOT_RELIABLE.
Execution cost drag (40 per order across 8 legs round trip + 1.5% slippage per fill) exceeds the collected credit in normal-rich zones, leaving no net edge even when pinning behaves as hypothesized.
EOD single-timestamp OI walls diverge from settlement-week wall evolution, so the max-pain anchor drifts and the pinning advantage disappears.
records.hypothesis: NIFTY weekly settlement gravitates toward max pain and heavy OI walls (documented pinning: spot closes within a few points of max pain and OI walls cap the move). A defined-risk broken-wing condor whose short legs are anchored to the max-pain strike and the nearest OI walls, instead of a symmetric spot-based grid, sits on the settlement magnet rather than the mid. Entering only when the regime gate reports TREND_HV with India VIX >= 16 (rich-to-high premium zone) pays the seller for high-volatility premium while OI gravity pulls spot back toward the anchor over the weekly horizon. The asymmetric wing design caps tail risk on the trend-away side at a declared width while the premium-collecting side hugs the dense wall. It may fail because TREND_HV is a trending regime: the same flow that builds the walls can blow through them at expiry, and EOD single-timestamp walls may not represent settlement-week dynamics. No profitability claim is made here; the frozen engine, the canonical expiry calendar and the canonical cost model decide.
records.research_question: On the frozen window, for NIFTY weeklies, does a broken-wing condor with short legs anchored to max pain and OI walls, entered only when REGIME == TREND_HV, VIX >= 16 and PCR <= 0.95, deliver positive mean net P&L per trade after the canonical 40 per order and 1.5% per-fill slippage cost model over at least 20 trades, and is its worst-trade loss bounded by the declared wide-wing maximum loss on every entry?
records.title: Max-pain and OI-wall anchored broken-wing condor, gated on TREND_HV with VIX >= 16 and call-heavy PCR
